item.title: Where Brazil’s Left Is Losing Voters
item.description: Far from Rio and São Paulo, small towns like Nanuque, with big agricultural businesses and a surging evangelical Christian movement, are swinging to the right.
item.dc:creator: Adam B. Ellick, Seth Kugel and Jeb Banegas
item.media:credit: Seth Kugel for The New York Times

item.title: Trump’s Tariffs Slow America’s Access to Canada’s Cheese
item.description: The Trump administration’s tariffs are slowing Americans’ access to the cheese just as producers were finding a foothold stateside.
item.dc:creator: Pete Wells

item.title: As Brazil Prepares for Election Runoff, a Town Offers Clues to Bolsonaro’s Rise
item.description: Deep in cattle country, voter sentiments in an evangelical stronghold help explain why the country’s leftist president is the underdog in Sunday’s election.
item.dc:creator: Adam B. Ellick and Seth Kugel
item.media:credit: Seth Kugel for The New York Times
item.media:description: A gathering last month in Nanuque, Brazil, where longtime residents and those who have moved away come together to dance and reconnect.

item.title: The Bukeleization of Latin America Has Arrived
item.description: Nayib Bukele’s notoriously harsh and wildly popular security crackdown in El Salvador is spawning imitators and remaking the region.
item.dc:creator: Jack Nicas
item.media:credit: Fred Ramos for The New York Times
item.media:description: President Nayib Bukele of El Salvador has overseen an extraordinary security crackdown that has led to plummeting crime rates.

item.title: Space Debris Found Twice Within Days Amid ‘Growing Casualty Risk’
item.description: Debris was found in Indonesia on Monday, just days after a farmer across the globe in Minnesota reported a massive metal object thought to be space junk in a cornfield.
item.dc:creator: Ephrat Livni
item.media:credit: Ahmad Syihab/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: A large charred metallic fragment, suspected to be rocket debris, at an oil palm plantation in East Kotawaringin Regency, in Indonesia’s Central Kalimantan province, in October.

item.title: El Salvador’s President Issues Harsh Warning to Haitian Gangs After 4 Soldiers Are Abducted
item.description: Four members of El Salvador’s military were abducted Sunday in Haiti, and their president wants them back.

item.title: Thélyson Orélien's Quebec Publisher Cuts Ties Over A.I. Accusations

item.title: A.I. Election Videos Are Flooding Brazil. Could They Sway the Vote?
item.description: Brazil spent years targeting electoral lies on the internet. Now, artificial intelligence is stumping the election authorities and reshaping a high-stakes race.
item.dc:creator: Ana Ionova

item.title: Death Toll From Venezuela Quakes Likely Far Exceeds Official Count
item.description: A Times analysis and U.S. Geological Survey data indicate that the official 6,509 death toll is probably a severe undercount.
item.dc:creator: James Glanz, Julie Turkewitz and Helmuth Rosales
item.media:credit: Adriana Loureiro Fernandez for The New York Times
item.media:description: Volunteers and relatives searching for bodies in the rubble of a public housing complex that collapsed during the twin earthquakes in July.

item.title: Why These Towers Collapsed in Venezuela’s Earthquakes
item.description: A 3-D reconstruction reveals why multiple apartment towers toppled in the earthquakes that struck Venezuela in June. Our reporter Julie Turkewitz examines how structural flaws — not just the strength of the quakes — left the towers vulnerable to collapse.
item.dc:creator: Julie Turkewitz, James Glanz, Helmuth Rosales, Leila Medina, Thomas Vollkommer, James Surdam, Joey Sendaydiego and Adriana Loureiro Fernandez

item.title: As Alberta Rejects Canada Separatism, Carney Gets Much of the Credit

item.media:credit: Todd Korol/Reuters
item.media:description: Prime Minister Mark Carney of Canada, center, with supporters of Alberta’s staying in Canada in Red Deer, Alberta, last Friday.

item.title: Flamingo Birdnapping in Las Vegas Ends With a Cruelty Conviction
item.description: The man, visiting from Canada, carried a flamingo named Peachy from its habitat to his hotel room. He was convicted of felony and misdemeanor charges.

item.media:description: The man convicted in the case, Mitchell Fairbarn, left, in court with his lawyer, Josh Tomsheck.

item.title: The Mayor of a City in Haiti Warned of a Massacre. No One Listened.
item.description: The mayor of Kenscoff, a town near Haiti’s capital, wrote government officials hundreds of letters to warn of gang threats. Then dozens of people died, and he did, too.
item.dc:creator: Frances Robles
item.media:credit: Michael Anthony Adams/The New York Times
item.media:description: The former mayor of Kenscoff, Haiti, Jean Massillon, showing bullet holes outside Kenscoff City Hall after a gang attack in August that killed 47 people. He died two weeks after this photo was taken.

item.title: 14 Dead After Gold Mine Collapses in Colombia

item.media:description: An illegal gold mine in Bajo Cauca area in Antioquia, Colombia, this year.

item.title: Visitor Killed by Roof Debris at Frank Lloyd Wright’s Taliesin West
